blocks.content: The Maratha Empire played a crucial role in Indian history after the decline of the Mughal Empire. It was founded by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in the 17th century. Shivaji established a strong administrative system and a powerful military.
1. Background of the Maratha Power

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Shivaji Maharaj established an independent Maratha kingdom, crowned as Chhatrapati at Raigad Fort in 1674.
The Maratha administration was governed by the Ashta Pradhan, a council of eight key ministers led by the Peshwa.
Military strategy relied heavily on guerrilla warfare (Ganimi Kava) and a network of strategic hill forts.
Revenue was augmented by dual taxation on neighboring regions: Chauth (1/4th revenue) and Sardeshmukhi (10% additional levy).
Internal factionalism and the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) contributed to the eventual decline of the Maratha power.

blocks.content: • The Marathas lived in the Deccan region of India.
• They were mainly farmers and warriors.
• The weakening of the Deccan Sultanates and Mughal authority helped the rise of Maratha power.
• Shivaji organized the Marathas into a strong military and political force.
2. Shivaji Maharaj (1630–1680)
Shivaji was the founder of the Maratha Empire and one of the greatest rulers in Indian history.
3. Early Conquests of Shivaji
• Captured Torna Fort in 1646.
• Captured several forts in the Deccan region.
• Defeated Afzal Khan, a general of Bijapur Sultanate.
• Established control over many strategic forts.
4. Conflict with the Mughals
• Shivaji fought several battles against Mughal forces.
Chapter 8: Maratha Empire and Shivaji
• He attacked Surat in 1664.
• He was invited to the Mughal court by Aurangzeb but later escaped from Agra in 1666.
5. Administration of Shivaji
6. Military System
• Shivaji organized a strong and disciplined army.
• He developed a powerful navy to protect the western coast.
• He used guerrilla warfare tactics known as 'Ganimi Kava'.

rows: Collected from foreign/neighboring territories to safeguard them against Maratha raids.
Claimed on grounds of hereditary overlordship (Sardeshmukh) over the Maharashtra region.

blocks.content: 7. Revenue System
• Land revenue was the main source of income.
• Two important taxes were collected:
• Chauth – one-fourth of revenue collected from territories.
• Sardeshmukhi – additional tax collected from regions.
8. Expansion after Shivaji
• After Shivaji's death, the Maratha Empire expanded further under the Peshwas.
• Peshwa Baji Rao I greatly expanded Maratha territory.
• The Marathas became a major political power in India.
9. Decline of the Maratha Empire
• The Third Battle of Panipat in 1761 weakened the Marathas.

items: Ashta Pradhan Ministers: Frequently asked in SSC exams (e.g., Peshwa = Prime Minister, Amatya = Finance Minister, Sumant = Foreign Affairs).
Treaty of Purandar (1665): Signed between Shivaji Maharaj and Jai Singh I representing Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb.
Taxation Distinctions: SSC questions often contrast Chauth (25% protection fee) with Sardeshmukhi (10% hereditary claim).

SSC Exam Important Facts
• Shivaji was crowned in 1674 at Raigad.
• The council of ministers was called Ashta Pradhan.
• Shivaji used guerrilla warfare tactics.
• Chauth and Sardeshmukhi were Maratha taxes.
• Third Battle of Panipat (1761) weakened Maratha power.
